indications.name: Removable oral appliances for obstructive sleep apnea

criteria.text: Evaluated before treatment, in person or by telemedicine, by a qualified physician or a physician-supervised Advanced Practice Provider who diagnoses OSA and recommends the course of treatment
OSA documented by a sleep study such as attended polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing
Treating physician or Advanced Practice Provider documents that PAP therapy had no therapeutic efficacy, or that the individual is intolerant of or has refused PAP
Meets the InterQual CP Durable Medical Equipment, Noninvasive Airway Assistive Devices criteria for removable oral appliances

indications.name: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty, mandibular osteotomy, and maxillomandibular osteotomy and advancement in adults

criteria.text: Evaluated before treatment, in person or by telemedicine, by a qualified physician or a physician-supervised Advanced Practice Provider who diagnoses OSA and recommends the course of treatment
Moderate to severe OSA with AHI ≥ 15 or RDI ≥ 15 on attended polysomnography
Excessive daytime sleepiness documented with an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score above 10 or another validated tool
PAP therapy had no therapeutic efficacy, or the individual refused or is intolerant of PAP
For maxillomandibular osteotomy and advancement, craniofacial disproportion or deformities with evidence of maxillomandibular deficiency
For mandibular osteotomy, retrolingual or lower pharyngeal function obstruction

indications.name: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation in adults with moderate to severe OSA

criteria.text: Evaluated before treatment, in person or by telemedicine, by a qualified physician or a physician-supervised Advanced Practice Provider who diagnoses OSA and recommends the course of treatment
BMI ≤ 40 kg/m²
AHI of at least 15 on a sleep study
Central and mixed apneas are less than 25% of the total AHI on attended polysomnography
No complete blockage or complete concentric collapse of the soft palate on drug-induced sleep endoscopy
PAP therapy had no therapeutic efficacy, or the individual refused or is intolerant of PAP
FDA-approved device used in accordance with FDA guidelines

indications.name: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation in adolescents aged 10 to 18 years with Down syndrome

criteria.text: Evaluated before treatment, in person or by telemedicine, by a qualified physician or a physician-supervised Advanced Practice Provider who diagnoses OSA and recommends the course of treatment
Severe OSA with AHI ≥ 10 and RDI ≤ 50 events per hour on attended polysomnography
BMI below the 95th percentile for age
Central and mixed apneas are less than 25% of the total AHI
Contraindication for, or not effectively treated with, a prior adenotonsillectomy
Confirmed failure or intolerance of PAP therapy despite attempts to improve adherence
No tracheostomy use during sleep
No complete blockage or concentric collapse at the soft palate level on drug-induced sleep endoscopy
Individual and caregiver refuse an MMA procedure for nonconcentric palatal collapse
FDA-approved device used in accordance with FDA guidelines

exclusions: Nasal dilator devices for treating OSA
Intranasal expiratory resistance valve, such as Bongo Rx
Mandibular vertical repositioning devices, such as Slow Wave
Epigenetic appliances, such as Homeoblock or DNA (Daytime/Nighttime appliance)
Lingual suspension, also called tongue stabilization, tongue stitch, or tongue fixation
Implantable phrenic nerve stimulation devices, such as the remedē System, for central sleep apnea
Removable oral appliances for treating central sleep apnea
documentation_requirements: A sleep study documenting OSA, such as attended polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing, for removable oral appliances
Documentation from the treating physician or Advanced Practice Provider that PAP therapy had no therapeutic efficacy, or that the individual is intolerant of or has refused PAP
Excessive daytime sleepiness documented with an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score above 10 or another validated tool
Repeat polysomnography if there has been clinically significant weight loss or gain, a change in cardiovascular disease, or persistent or recurrent symptoms since the last study
Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage
